name: Stope design and release
summary: Before a block of ore between two sub-levels can be drilled and blasted, the engineers produce a stope package: the mineable shape around the vein, the longhole drill rings, the blasting, mucking, ventilation and backfill instructions, and the ground support. Geology supplies the ore outline from face samples and definition drill holes, a surveyor picks up the as-built sub-levels, the mine planning engineer designs the shape and rings, the single geotechnical engineer checks spans and cable bolting, and geology, engineering and operations sign the package before the surveyor marks the collars and it is handed to the longhole crew. Work queues behind the few people on a 14-on, 14-off rotation, and new assays that move the vein edge send designs back for rework.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer running a 500-650 tpd narrow-vein underground mine in northern Ontario, with a technical services department of about 20 engineers, surveyors and geologists on a 14-on, 14-off rotation.
baseline.notes: Practice follows the Eagle River mine technical reports (2016, 2022) and the neighbouring Island Gold report (2020); software is AutoCAD with Promine, Microsoft Access drillhole database, Excel workbooks and email, with Deswik and Leapfrog arriving in 2021.

trigger: The monthly mine plan schedules a stope (one sub-level block of a stope panel) for drilling in the coming weeks, or a released stope must be redesigned.
end_state: A signed stope package is filed and handed to the longhole crew with ring collars marked, or the stope is deferred because it does not pay.

volume.seasonality: Even through the year; a burst of redesigns follows the annual reserve model update in the first quarter.

evidence.note: About 81% of mill feed (13,300 t a month at 16,400 t) comes from stopes (er2022). A sub-level block between rib pillars of 15 m height, 20-30 m strike and 2.5 m diluted width holds about 2,000-2,800 t at 2.7 t/m3, giving 5 to 7 packages a month; this agrees with the organisation file's 4-9 (mode 6).

surge.cause: Annual mineral reserve and resource model update (and the 2021 move from polygonal to 3D estimation) changes ore outlines and cut-offs, so queued stopes are redesigned

evidence.note: er2022 describes the reserve update and the 2021 change to 3D estimation; the size and length of the redesign burst are the author's estimate.
Production engineering designs mineable stope shapes and packages (island); 9 mine engineering staff (er2022 Table 16-10). FTE share is the author's estimate from per-package times.
Geology creates the resource shapes passed to engineering (island). FTE share is the author's estimate.
Stability graph checks and cable bolt needs at stope design (potvin; island uses the Matthews stability graph). One geotechnical engineer per the organisation file.
As-built pick-up of sub-levels and marking of ring collars is common practice; not listed among the process roles in the organisation file. FTE share is the author's estimate.
Chief engineer sign-off is common practice; not listed among the process roles in the organisation file.
Operations sign the package; most mines have a sign-off that includes management (potvin).

systems.name: Mine design and scheduling software (3D design, scheduling)
Total stations, cavity monitoring scanner and survey software
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)

resources.name: Underground utility fleet (scissor lifts and light vehicles)

steps.name: Open the design request from the monthly plan
steps.description: The mine planning engineer picks the next stope from the monthly plan's list of stopes due for drilling, opens the design folder and checks which sub-levels, raises and cable bolting are already done. Requests queue behind other designs and the engineer's days off the rotation.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of queue time with one to two planning engineers on site at a time.

steps.name: Compile the geology outline for the stope block
steps.description: The mine geologist gathers the chip sample composites from the sub-levels, the definition drill holes and the face maps for the block, and draws the vein outline and grade on sections and the longitudinal section. This resource shape is passed to engineering as the starting point for the design.

error.defect_description: Outline drawn from stale assays or extended too far between drill holes.

evidence.note: Resource shapes created by geology then submitted to production engineering (island); sub-levels and definition holes on vein (er2022). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide whether drill coverage is enough
steps.description: The geologist checks the spacing of drill holes and sampled sub-levels against the stope outline. Where the vein edge or a fault offset is not known, the geologist asks for infill definition holes before the design goes further.

evidence.note: If required, definition diamond drilling is completed ahead of the stope design work (potvin). Share needing infill is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for infill drilling and assays
steps.description: The diamond drilling contractor drills the extra holes from the nearest drill bay, the core is logged and sampled, and the assays come back from the lab. The design waits until the outline can be redrawn.

evidence.note: Two to four weeks for drill scheduling, drilling, logging and assays is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Drive to the stope sub-levels
steps.description: A surveyor books a light vehicle and travels down the ramp to the stope's haulage level and, for captive sub-levels, climbs through the Alimak raise to reach the sub-levels. The surveyor and vehicle are shared with month-end surveys and development lines.

evidence.note: Captive sub-levels are reached only through the Alimak raise (er2022); travel and wait times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Survey the as-built sub-levels
steps.description: The surveyor picks up the walls, backs and brows of each sub-level and the raise with a total station, so the design uses where the drifts really are rather than where they were planned. Before working in the raise and captive sub-levels the surveyor checks the workplace and ground support.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854: workplace examination and ground support check before work; site procedure for travel in Alimak raises and captive sub-levels

evidence.note: As-built survey of stope development is common practice; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Process the survey into the design model
steps.description: Back on surface the surveyor downloads the instrument, builds the as-built drift outlines and adds them to the mine model in AutoCAD and Promine. The engineer is told the as-builts are ready.

error.defect_description: Station error or wrong level datum shifts the as-built drifts.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Design the mineable stope shape
steps.description: The engineer wraps a mineable shape around the vein outline with at least 1.5 m mining width, adds 0.5 m of hangingwall and 0.5 m of footwall dilution, places rib and sill pillars, and calculates diluted tonnes and grade with 90% mining recovery. Waste needed for the broken ore to flow to the drawpoints is added as planned dilution.
outputs: stope shape with tonnes and grade

error.defect_description: Dilution or pillar placement understated, so the stope grade is overstated.

evidence.note: Minimum width, dilution skin from CMS reconciliation, 90% recovery and must-take waste (er2022). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the stope pays at the cut-off grade
steps.description: The engineer compares the diluted grade with the 5.5 g/t stope cut-off and looks at the marginal blocks at the ends. Stopes that do not pay are deferred; marginal ones go back to geology for a second look at the outline.
inputs: stope shape with tonnes and grade

evidence.note: Stope cut-off 5.5 g/t (er2022); economic viability evaluated on each stope shape (island). Shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess spans, pillars and cable bolting
steps.description: The geotechnical engineer checks the stope's hangingwall and back spans on the Matthews stability graph using Q' and N' for the sheared diorite walls, compares with overbreak measured by cavity surveys in nearby stopes, and specifies cable bolts for the walls and brows. With one geotechnical engineer on a rotation, this review is the usual bottleneck.
inputs: stope shape with tonnes and grade

evidence.note: Stability graph and cable bolt assessment (island, potvin); sheared diorite as the main dilution source and cable bolting of walls (er2022). Times and wait are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide whether the shape must change
steps.description: From the assessment the geotechnical engineer either accepts the shape or asks the engineer to shorten the stope, add a rib pillar or change the sequence so a long open span is not left waiting for fill.

next.condition: span too large: shorten stope or add pillar

evidence.note: Hangingwall dilution increasing with depth needs smaller stopes or more rib pillars, and uncemented fill leaves large open spans (er2022). Rework share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Design the drill rings and slot
steps.description: The engineer lays out the longhole rings for each sub-level: 64 mm down-holes 13 to 18 m long on a 3-2-3 pattern with 0.9 m burden and 1.2 m spacing, up-holes at 70 degrees for the sill pillar, and the slot raise at the far end. Ring drawings with collar positions, hole lengths and angles are printed for the drillers.
inputs: stope shape with tonnes and grade

error.defect_description: Collar or hole angle error makes holes miss the vein edge or over-drill into the hangingwall.

evidence.note: Drilling pattern, hole lengths and up-hole angle (er2022, er2016). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write the blast, mucking, ventilation and fill directives
steps.description: The engineer writes the blast letter (stick emulsion loading, delays, retreat sequence from the slot back to the raise), the shrink-mucking instructions that leave broken ore in the stope until the last blast, the ventilation and gas-check instructions, and whether a cemented rockfill sill mat is needed before uncemented fill. These go into the package with the tonnes, grade and drawings.

evidence.note: Package contents: drilling plans, blast letters, ventilation and gas check instructions, mucking plans and backfilling directives (island); shrink mucking and CRF sill mats (er2022); design note contents (potvin).

steps.name: Geology reviews and signs the package
steps.description: The mine geologist checks that the stope outline and grade still match the latest face and drill assays and signs the package. If new assays have moved the vein edge, the shape goes back for rework.

control.basis: Site stope release procedure: geology, engineering, geotechnical and operations signatures before drilling

next.condition: new assays change the outline: redesign

evidence.note: Sign-off by specialist disciplines (potvin); rework share is the author's estimate of the 'common' rework named in the organisation file.

steps.name: Geotechnical engineer signs the package
steps.description: The geotechnical engineer checks that the cable bolt pattern, pillars and sequence in the final package match the assessment and signs it. Designs wait when the engineer is on days off.

control.basis: Site ground control program under Ontario Regulation 854: stope spans, pillars and support designed and approved by a qualified engineer

evidence.note: Geotechnical review and sign-off of stope designs (potvin; stephenson).

steps.name: Chief engineer reviews and signs
steps.description: The technical services manager reads the package against the monthly plan and sequence, checks tonnes, grade and fill timing, and signs or asks for changes to the drilling or sequence.

control.basis: Site stope release procedure: engineering approval

evidence.note: Sign-off includes management (potvin; stephenson). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Operations reviews and signs
steps.description: The mine superintendent, usually with the mine captain, checks that the drill can be slung to the sub-levels, the drawpoints and remucks suit the LHDs, and the timing fits the crews, then signs. Access or equipment problems send the rings back for change.

control.basis: Site stope release procedure: operations approval

evidence.note: Operations sign-off (potvin); small longhole drills slung through the Alimak raise (er2022). Rework share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Drive underground to mark out the stope
steps.description: The surveyor takes the signed ring drawings and a light vehicle to the stope and climbs to each sub-level. The trip waits for a free vehicle and a day when the sub-level is not being cable bolted.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Mark ring lines and slot collars
steps.description: The surveyor paints the ring lines on the walls and back and marks the slot raise and collar positions so the longhole driller sets up on the design. Sub-levels still being cleaned or bolted are marked on a later visit.

evidence.note: Ring mark-up by survey is common practice; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hand over the released package
steps.description: The engineer files the signed package, emails it to the mine captain and longhole drillers and walks them through the rings, slot and blast sequence at the start of shift. The stope is then released for drilling, and the design goes to the geotechnical file for later comparison with the cavity survey.

evidence.note: Signed-off design is the main input to execution and later CMS reconciliation (potvin).

exceptions.name: Infill drilling needed
exceptions.description: Gaps in drill coverage hold the design for two to four weeks of drilling and assays.

exceptions.name: New assays move the vein edge
exceptions.description: Face or drill assays that arrive after the shape is drawn send the package back to the shape design.

exceptions.name: Span too large
exceptions.description: The geotechnical check shortens the stope or adds a rib pillar.

exceptions.name: Stope does not pay
exceptions.description: The diluted grade is below the cut-off and the stope is deferred.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from stope scheduled in the plan to package released

evidence.note: For mines with small rapid-turnaround stopes the design steps are completed within a few weeks, against about three months at large stopes (potvin); the p50 and p90 are the author's reading of 'a few weeks'.

benchmarks.unit: metres of wall overbreak (0.5 m hangingwall plus 0.5 m footwall)
benchmarks.population: Eagle River stopes measured by cavity monitoring surveys

benchmarks.unit: share of designed stope tonnes recovered

pain_points.description: One geotechnical engineer on a 14-on, 14-off rotation reviews and signs every stope, so packages wait for the engineer's return.

evidence.note: Single geotechnical engineer per the organisation file; wait times are the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: New face and drill assays arrive while the design is in progress and move the vein edge, sending the shape and rings back for rework.

evidence.note: Feedback loops and late orebody updates are described in potvin; the organisation file names this rework as common.

pain_points.description: Designs pass through several programs (Promine, survey software, spreadsheets, later Deswik), and comparing designs with cavity surveys means re-keying between them.

evidence.note: Multiple software packages make stope design and reconciliation slow (potvin); the move to Deswik was in progress (er2022).

pain_points.description: Hangingwall dilution from the sheared diorite grows with depth and uncemented fill leaves large open spans, which pushes designs toward smaller stopes and more pillars.

assumptions: One case is one sub-level block of a stope panel between rib pillars; a full panel of three sub-levels may be released in two or three packages.
The geotechnical assessment (s10, s11) is the same work as the ts-geotech process triggered by stope_design; count it once when assembling the organisation model.
Surveyors (as-builts and collar mark-up) and the technical services manager (sign-off) take part, although the organisation file's process entry lists neither.
The simulated cycle time adds waits in sequence; the survey trip (s05-s07) in practice overlaps the geology outline (s02), so the simulated median runs a little longer than the benchmark.
Drill and blast details follow the captive sub-level open stoping method of the reference mine; mechanised sub-levels skip the raise climb but follow the same steps.
Loaded costs per hour are taken from the organisation file.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (CAPR001445)
sources.publisher: SRK Consulting (Canada) Inc. for Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd.
sources.supports: Reference mine practice: channel (chip) sampling of underground faces by production geologist and technician after each advance once the heading is inspected and supported, sample lengths 0.3 m minimum in ore and 0.3 m maximum with visible gold; test-hole, long-hole and muck sampling (one muck sample per 25-30 t truck, taken by muckers); samples brought to surface at end of the beat geologist's shift and shuttled daily to the company assay office in Wawa; mine lab not accredited, 11% QC insertion (blank, CRM, duplicate per 28-sample tray), VG protocol, low-grade CRM bias; channel results recorded in Promine; polygonal estimates before 2021, Leapfrog/Datamine 3D model from 2021; chip samples average higher than core; mine-to-mill reconciliation within 5%; stope design with 1.5 m minimum width, 0.5 m HW and FW dilution from CMS reconciliation, 90% stope and 99% development recovery, stope cut-off 5.5 g/t, development cut-off 2.0 g/t, density 2.7 t/m3; captive sub-level open stoping via Alimak raises, 13-18 m 64 mm down-holes on a 3-2-3 pattern, shrink mucking, CRF sill mats and URF fill; 19% of mill feed from sill development; ore hoisted in 4 t skips and trucked 16.6 km from the portal pad to the mill; two 12 h shifts 365 days a year; UG labour table with 9 mine engineering and 10 mine geology staff; recommendation to evaluate tools for short-term planning; ventilation rule 0.06 m3/s per kW of diesel

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Mining Complex including the Eagle River Gold Mine, the Mishi Gold Mine and Related Infrastructure
sources.publisher: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. (G. Mannard and P. Ng), hosted by minedocs.com
sources.supports: Chip samples taken every round (every 3 to 4 m) in ore development headings across the full face, about 2.5 kg, 0.3-0.5 m lengths; raises sometimes chip sampled and always muck sampled; muck sample per 25-30 t; sealed samples transported daily to the company Mine Assay office with results emailed to the mine; assay data in Microsoft Access linked to Promine and Surpac/Gemcom, databases updated weekly and audited monthly; about 30% of production from silling and development; CMS surveys show about 1.0 m wall overbreak; Mishi grade control on blast hole samples

sources.title: NI 43-101 Technical Report for the Island Gold Mine, Dubreuilville, Ontario, Canada (exhibit 99.1)
sources.publisher: Alamos Gold Inc. (filed on SEC EDGAR)
sources.supports: Neighbouring Wawa-area mine: resource shapes created by geology and passed to production engineering for mineable stope design with recovery and dilution factors; each stope gets a package with drilling plans, blast letters, ventilation and gas check instructions, mucking plans and backfilling directives; Matthews stability graph used for stope dimensions; CMS surveys and beat geologists control dilution while mucking; chip samples 1.5-2 kg taken by geological technician or geologist, assays entered into Promine; all underground production samples assayed at the Wesdome laboratory in Wawa; 2019 production reconciled to mill was 107% of tonnes, 98% of grade and 105% of ounces of the current reserve model, with monthly comparison going forward

sources.title: Benchmarking of stope design and reconciliation practices (Underground Mining Technology 2020)
sources.publisher: Australian Centre for Geomechanics (Y. Potvin, K.R. Woodward, B. McFadyen, I. Thin, D. Grant)
sources.supports: 2019 workshops in Perth and Rouyn-Noranda with 19 underground mines: stope design note contents (shape, wireframe, ground support, slot and rings, fill, ventilation, predicted overbreak); definition drilling completed ahead of design if needed; design about three months before extraction at large stopes and within a few weeks at small rapid-turnaround stopes; drill and blast design a few days before drilling; most mines have a comprehensive sign-off involving geotechnical, backfill, ventilation and management; stope reconciliation starts with CMS; all mines reconcile volume, tonnes and grade per stope and feed a periodic mine reconciliation led by geology; multiple software packages make reconciliation slow; narrow vein mines focus on hangingwall overbreak and ELOS

sources.title: Optimising stope design and ground support: a case study (Ground Support 2013)
sources.publisher: Australian Centre for Geomechanics (R.M. Stephenson and M.P. Sandy, AMC Consultants)
sources.supports: At a Western Australian underground gold mine, geotechnical engineers review stope designs with planning engineers, followed by a sign-off process documenting the conclusions for management approval and a team-based risk assessment for each stope
